name: research-match
description: MCP server that connects isolated researchers via AI originality scoring and bilateral matching.
long_description:
Research Match is an MCP server that helps researchers find complementary collaborators while protecting intellectual property. It uses AI-powered originality scoring on two independent axes (Theoretical Originality and Formal-Computational Originality) and bilateral matching with a semaphore system (GREEN/YELLOW/RED) that shows each researcher what they gain from a potential collaboration.

**KEY FEATURES**
- **AI Originality Scoring**: Dual-axis evaluation (OT/OFC) with solidity multipliers (proven, functional, speculative, adhoc, cherry_picked)
- **Bilateral Matching**: Complementarity-based matching with perspective-aware reasoning — each side sees gains from their own viewpoint
- **Privacy by Design**: Emails are SHA-256 hashed, pseudonymous identities, no raw content shared until collaboration is accepted
- **Reputation System**: Anti-retaliation ratings (anonymous until both rate), exponential smoothing, honesty-weighted
- **Cold Search**: Free search across internal DB and GitHub — no registration required
- **Semantic Similarity**: sentence-transformers embeddings with Jaccard fallback

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS**
- Python 3.12 or higher
- UV Package Manager
This MCP server requires UV, a fast Python package manager.
Installation:
`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`
For detailed installation instructions, [see the UV documentation](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)

database_path.title: Database Path
database_path.description: Path to the SQLite database file. Leave empty to use the default (research_match.db in the extension directory).

tools.name: research_match_register
tools.description: STEP 1 — Register with a pseudonymous identity. Email is SHA-256 hashed and never stored in plain text. Idempotent: safe to call multiple times.

tools.name: research_match_analyze_work
tools.description: HELPER — Get the Research Commit template before submitting. Returns structured template with all fields and solidity guide.

tools.name: research_match_submit_commit
tools.description: STEP 2 — Submit a structured Research Commit for AI originality evaluation on two axes: Theoretical Originality (OT) and Formal-Computational Originality (OFC).

tools.name: research_match_my_profile
tools.description: View your Research Match profile: reputation, scores, commit history, and team memberships.

tools.name: research_match_find_collaborators
tools.description: STEP 3 — Find researchers with complementary skills. Returns candidates with bilateral semaphore (GREEN/YELLOW/RED) and perspective-aware reasoning.

tools.name: research_match_send_request
tools.description: STEP 4 — Send a collaboration request to a matched researcher. The recipient sees scores from their own perspective.

tools.name: research_match_inbox
tools.description: View all collaboration requests — incoming and outgoing — with semaphore, scores, and status.

tools.name: research_match_respond_request
tools.description: Accept or reject an incoming collaboration request. Acceptance creates a team with joint-equal licensing (50/50).

tools.name: research_match_rate_user
tools.description: Rate a collaborator on honesty, quality, and effort (1-5 each). Ratings are anonymous until both members rate.

tools.name: research_match_cold_search
tools.description: FREE cold search — no registration required. Searches internal DB and GitHub for research topics.
